name: Fête de l’Alicoque — new olive oil
summary: Nyons celebrates the season’s first pressing — bread rubbed with new oil on the square, mills open, producers everywhere.

name: Truffle season & Richerenches market
summary: The Rhône’s black-gold season: the famous Saturday wholesale market, truffle menus in local restaurants, and the January truffle mass.

name: Apricot & orchard blossom
summary: The Baronnies are apricot country — for a few weeks the valleys around Saint-Jalle turn pink and white. Best light in the morning.

name: Fête de la Transhumance
summary: Thousands of sheep flood through Die’s streets on their way to Vercors summer pastures — shepherd culture, markets and music.

name: Lavender in bloom
summary: The purple weeks: fields around Grignan, the Ferrassières plateau and Sault at their peak. Go early or late for the light — and the bees.

name: Fêtes nocturnes de Grignan
summary: Open-air theatre on the château terrace with the lit castle as backdrop — one of the Drôme’s magical summer evenings.

name: Fête du Tilleul
summary: Buis honours its linden-blossom heritage — once Europe’s tilleul capital — with a market, music and plenty of herbal everything.

name: Les Olivades
summary: Nyons’ summer olive festival — tastings, producers, music and the old town at its liveliest.

name: Festival d’Avignon
summary: One of the world’s great theatre festivals takes over the whole city — hundreds of shows a day, street performers everywhere.

name: Chorégies d’Orange
summary: Opera under the stars in a 2,000-year-old Roman theatre with legendary acoustics — bucket-list stuff.

name: Vaison Danses
summary: International dance companies perform in Vaison’s Roman theatre — a more intimate cousin of the Orange spectacle.

name: Village night markets
summary: Marchés nocturnes pop up across the villages on summer evenings — producers, crafts, rosé and long tables under the plane trees.

name: Fête de la Lavande
summary: Sault’s big lavender day — sickle-harvest contests, parades and lavender in every form, high on the plateau.

name: Harvest & open cellars
summary: Vendange time: the wine villages buzz, cellars pour the new vintage, and many domaines hold open days and harvest lunches.

name: Christmas & santon markets
summary: Provençal Christmas: santon (crib figure) fairs, village markets, vin chaud and the 13 desserts tradition.

name: Sunday antiques & brocante market
summary: The antiques capital of Provence: every Sunday the canal-side quays fill with brocante stalls, on top of the town’s permanent antique-dealer villages.

name: International antiques fairs
summary: Twice a year the Sunday market explodes into one of Europe’s biggest antiques fairs — hundreds of extra dealers from all over the continent.

name: Flea market (marché aux puces)
summary: The region’s classic Saturday puces on Place Charles David — proper flea-market rummaging, from real finds to charming junk.

name: Village vide-greniers (rommelmarkten)
summary: Almost every village holds a vide-grenier — the whole town empties its attics onto the square. Small, cheap and full of surprises; a new one somewhere every weekend.

name: Brocante corners at the big weekly markets
summary: The great Provençal weekly markets usually have a brocante/vintage section tucked at one end — arrive before 10 for the good stuff.
